name: Corneal Piezoelectric Delamination Pistol
description:
The CPDP-1 operates by projecting a tightly focused piezoelectric pulse tuned to the resonant frequency of corneal collagen lamellae. Upon contact with the eye, the pulse induces rapid micro-shear between successive corneal layers, causing progressive delamination from the epithelium down through the Bowman's layer. The effect manifests within seconds as a spreading opaque whitening across the target's visual field — irreversible without immediate surgical intervention.

What distinguishes the Milkscreen from simple blinding agents is its surgical precision and deniability. Unlike chemical or laser-based ocular weapons, it leaves no detectable residue and produces no visible beam. Victims frequently cannot identify the moment of attack, reporting only a sudden 'fogging' before full opacity sets in. The pistol format makes it concealable and deployable at conversational range, ideal for close-quarters operations where discretion is paramount.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric originally developed the CPDP-1 as a non-lethal compliance tool for detention facilities, marketing it as a 'temporary visual suppressor.' Field use quickly revealed the 'temporary' designation to be aspirational. Most victims require full corneal transplant to recover usable vision, and in GLMZ's tiered healthcare economy, that procedure is well beyond the means of most citizens.
specifications: effective range: 0.5–4 meters pulse frequency: 18.4 kHz (tuned to corneal collagen) charge per shot: 0.7 mJ battery capacity: 22 shots per cell dimensions: 14 cm length, 180g targeting: Passive IR ocular lock, manual override available housing: Matte polymer, passes most passive scanners
tactical_use: Deployed almost exclusively in close-range social infiltration scenarios — boardrooms, clubs, transit corridors. Operators typically fire once and withdraw, allowing the weapon's delayed onset to create distance between themselves and the incapacitation event. Effective for eliminating witness capacity without fatalities. Some interrogators use it as a coercive instrument, firing one shot and threatening the second.
cultural_context: The Milkscreen has acquired a particular dread in GLMZ's underworld because it is a weapon of humiliation as much as harm. Being 'screened' carries social stigma — it implies the victim was close enough to their attacker to be touched, that they were trusted into proximity. Corporate fixer circles use 'got their eyes done' as slang for a professional embarrassment. Street medics who can perform corneal grafts charge extortionate rates in districts where the weapon circulates.
known_users: Sable Rhen, a fixer known for leaving targets 'half-finished'
story_hooks: A witness to a high-profile corporate murder is found blind in a transit pod — no one in the carriage admits to seeing anything, and the weapon leaves no forensic trace.
A black-market corneal surgeon starts receiving death threats after becoming the only affordable option for Milkscreen victims in the Outerring districts.
A player character is hired to retrieve a stolen CPDP-1 prototype that fires a wider-dispersion pulse — potentially capable of blinding everyone in a standard office room.
A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric compliance officer is quietly selling decommissioned units through a shell distributor; someone wants proof, someone else wants the officer silenced.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, almost clinical handgun with an unusually elongated muzzle cap housing the piezoelectric resonance chamber. Silhouette suggests precision instrumentation rather than crude force — sleek, almost medical in appearance. The proportions feel deliberate and engineered for minimal visual disruption.
physical_description.dimensions: 14 cm length overall, 6 cm grip height, 3.2 cm width at slide. Muzzle cap extends 4 cm with subtle ribbed venting. 180g total mass.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light and well-balanced — feels more like a diagnostic tool than a weapon. Sits naturally in the palm without fatigue, weight distributed forward toward the precision chamber rather than rear.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-finish engineered polymer composite frame with internal piezoelectric ceramic matrix visible through subtle translucent sections. Slide appears to be brushed aerospace-grade aluminum.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal black polymer with brushed gunmetal accents. No gloss — intentionally designed to avoid light reflection. Subtle frosted treatment across grip reduces tactile signature.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant matte charcoal black with brushed silver-gray slide sections and minimal accent striping in pale cyan along the targeting reticle housing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Microtextured polymer with light grip angle — feels almost clinical, slightly cool to touch. Subtle ergonomic ridges rather than aggressive traction patterns. Minimal tactile feedback by design.
distinctive_features: Oversized muzzle cap with precision resonance chamber — 4cm ribbed extension housing piezoelectric discharge matrix
Passive IR targeting window recessed below the sights — glows faint amber during power-up
Translucent polymer sections revealing internal ceramic piezo stacks pulsing with faint bioluminescent charging indicators
Minimal sighting system — simple notch rear, bead front, optimized for close-quarters target acquisition
Weapon safe indicator: small cyan LED that extinguishes upon active lock
Micro heat-venting ports along the chamber collar — barely visible unless examined closely
Aggressive bevels and rounded edges throughout — designed to slip through conventional threat scanning systems
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC etched in micro-font along the left frame, barely legible. Serial plate sits flush beneath the slide on the right side — deliberately obscured during standard observation angles. No visible model designation on exterior.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn examples show minimal cosmetic damage but revealing signs of actual use: micro-scratches on the chamber vents from repeated cleaning, slight polymer stress marks near the trigger guard from high-frequency discharge cycling, occasional residual surface oxidation on the aluminum slide from moisture exposure. Operators keep them meticulously maintained — any mechanical failure risks exposure during the critical window between firing and withdrawal.
